title: When the Clock Burns
premise: In the river town of Vellacourt, 1848, Odile Eastwick helps her father cut type in a print shop that keeps more than one ledger: the official one for the army, and a hidden one of debts, favors, and names — including those of revolutionaries now declared enemies of the state. When soldiers requisition the shop and seize the public ledger, Odile discovers her father promised a dying printer-friend that his name would be struck from every record before the spring thaw, when tribunals begin. To honor it, she must forge type, bribe an old rival, and decide whether loyalty to the dead outweighs truth to the living. The book ends with Odile burning the hidden ledger herself on the breaking ice, saving one name at the cost of her father's freedom and her own innocence.
about_author: Beatrix Zhou is a former typesetting apprentice turned novelist who writes about ordinary people caught in history's machinery. She lives near a decommissioned print works and collects broken letterforms.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the Eastwick print shop, Odile learns to cut type while her father balances two ledgers — one for customers, one 'for the truth.' A sickly visitor leaves with a whispered promise from her father. Beat: cozy competence shadowed by secrets; Odile believes history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Soldiers occupy Vellacourt and commandeer the shop as a records office, seizing ledgers and presses. Father hides the second book inside a forme of locked type. Beat: violation and fear; the domestic world becomes military property overnight.

chapters.title: Names Are Heavy Things
chapters.summary: Father's POV. Interrogated about missing pages, he deflects a sharp clerk named Brissot while Odile eavesdrops. We learn the dead friend was a printer of banned pamphlets, now posthumously declared enemy. Beat: dread; the promise made in peacetime becomes a debt coming due.

chapters.title: The Ice Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She crosses the frozen river to the widow Roux, keeper of the friend's archive, and learns exactly which names must vanish before the thaw brings tribunals. Beat: resolve kindling; Odile stops being a bystander to other people's history.

chapters.title: An Old Rival's Price
chapters.summary: Father's POV. He approaches Maren Kessler, a rival typefounder with army contracts, to buy forged matrices. She demands the second ledger itself as payment. Beat: humiliation and calculation; loyalty begins costing something real.

chapters.title: What Brissot Knows
chapters.summary: Brissot's POV. The clerk, himself compromised by a brother among the rebels, notices the anomalous page counts but says nothing — yet. Beat: uneasy sympathy; the antagonist is revealed as another man surviving at a price.

chapters.title: The Night Sort
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Working by candlelight after curfew, she resets the seized record with altered names, nearly caught when a soldier returns for his forgotten pipe. Beat: terror and exhilaration; forgery as an act of love.

chapters.title: Kessler's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Father's POV. Kessler sells them out to save her own contracts; Brissot must arrest someone. Father takes the blame, claiming sole authorship of the forged entries. Beat: sacrifice; inheritance revealed as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: When the Clock Burns
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the tribunal on the eve of the thaw, Odile trades the second ledger — the true one, implicating half the town including Kessler — for her father's life, then hurls it onto the breaking ice where it burns and sinks. Beat: climax; truth destroyed to purchase mercy.

chapters.title: One Name Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, months later. The shop reopens under her hands; her father returns diminished, freed by a bargain no one will name. From the burned ledger she kept a single torn page — the friend's name — and sets it in type. Beat: bittersweet resolution; survival's price paid, memory preserved in metal.
